origin.source: HiRISE-identified rover at Bradbury Landing (ESP_028401_1755), in the CTX/MOLA-controlled frame (this project, M5)
origin.registration: Rover identified by eye in HiRISE ESP_028401_1755 (17 Aug 2012, eleven days after landing and five days before the first drive): a ~3 m object at the centre of the X-shaped scour left by the engines of the sky crane. That observation is uncontrolled, so its position was carried into controlled products by phase correlation of the surrounding terrain (consistent to ~2 m over nine sub-areas). The USGS HiRISE products here turned out to be offset from the CTX/MOLA-controlled frame (ESP_018854_1755 by 177 m, PSP_010573_1755 by 571 m, measured against the CTX controlled orthoimage), so the position is given in the CTX/MOLA frame: 20 m from NASA’s published Bradbury Landing coordinate (4.5895 S, 137.4417 E) and 85 m from the catalogue coordinate (4.59 S, 137.44 E; Seelos et al. 2014). The terrain under the rover is PSP_010573_1755 (2008, the only controlled HiRISE DTM covering this spot), sampled with its measured shift; being pre-landing, its ground image shows no blast marks.
